states.verdict: Same paper (#F9F9F9 in both), same 32px cap height, same 6px caret, line-height within 2px (76 vs 74) — so this comes down to the left edge, and A doesn't have one. Every time you drop a heading in A the text jumps 51-75px right, which you will feel as a lurch on every scroll pass through a long piece, and the permanent '188 words 961 characters 1 min read' strip is exactly the thing a drafting writer switches off. B's page is a straight line with the markup pushed out into the margin where it belongs, at a tighter 58ch to A's 62ch and 40px more side air. B's own failure is real and daily — text runs off the bottom rim with a sliced line and no scroll gutter — but a ragged reading edge is structural and a missing bottom pad is a setting.
